summary.value: The industrial stewards of the Molten Forge, who work alongside the ancient Lava-Core Colossus to produce farming tools, heating stones, and building materials for the realms. What the hero calls heavy ordnance is their machinery turned toward emergency defense — presses, pour-channels, and slag gates repurposed to slow an armed intruder.

sharedOpinions.reason: He smashed a week's pour of plowshares and called it dismantling a war machine. We will rebuild; we always rebuild.
Our heating stones warm their outlying homes. Fire workers keep faith with fire workers.
Half our safety drills are their curriculum. When a pour-channel bursts, a Heavy Hand is the second thing you see after the steam.

examples.value: Hot iron forgives nothing; neither does a hasty word.
A tool is judged by the hand it feeds, not the hand that swings it.

meaning.value: The scheduled casting runs that supply the realms' tools and heating stones. Stopping the pour mid-run is a genuine emergency.
The small stamped sigil on every tool and stone the forge ships. The hero's 'shards' often carry one — broken workshop enchantments, not evil.

customs.value: Every shift begins by naming what the day's work is for — a plow, a roof, a warming stone — so no one forgets the forge serves tables, not thrones.
Any moving machinery is announced with bell, banner, and marked floor. The Law of Fair Warning is the forge's oldest safety rule.

taboos.value: Never forge a weapon. The stewardry makes tools for living; the one time its machinery turned on a person, it was to drive him out, not to harm him.
Never quench a pour early out of panic. Cool it by the book, or someone colder than you pays for it downstream.
